scams.name: Mérida Airport (MID) Taxi & Pre-Paid-Only Overcharge Scam
scams.description: Mérida Airport (MID) is Yucatán's main gateway — small, efficient, 10 km from Centro Histórico (20 min drive) — but arrivals-kerb touts exploit the pre-paid-only taxi system. r/Yucatan 'merida airport to centro' (comments/1k0t3mx, 2025) is the canonical 2025 community anchor. r/Yucatan 'Merida airport question' (comments/1lrsbfq, 2025) and r/Yucatan 'Does the Merida airport allow you to get picked up by an' (comments/1ebkjlr) are 2025/2024 named anchors. r/Yucatan 'Uber cancel?' (comments/1k101kb, 2025) documents a 2025 Uber-availability quirk specific to MID. The legitimate fare: MID airport to Centro Histórico is MX$275–$350 via the official Transporte Terrestre prepaid booth inside arrivals; Uber is available BUT with limited airport pickup (Uber-Mérida has policy differences vs other cities); typical Uber rate MX$180–$250 if pickup works. The 2025 scams: (a) 'premium taxi' kiosks inside arrivals quoting MX$500–$800 flat rate (2–3x real Transporte Terrestre rate); (b) claim 'Uber doesn't work at MID' — Uber DOES work, but with meet-at-parking-lot-P2 limitation per r/Yucatan 'Uber cancel?' (comments/1k101kb, 2025); (c) arrivals-kerb 'hotel transfer' sign-holders at 2–3x real rate; (d) 'combined airport + Chichén Itzá day tour' bundled at MX$3,500 with excuse 'it's easier just one booking' — tour commission padded 80%+; (e) return-trip 'night surcharge' at MX$600 for departures before 6 AM (no such legitimate surcharge exists). For older travellers: (1) use the official Transporte Terrestre booth inside arrivals — MX$275–$350 flat-rate prepaid with printed receipt; this IS the safest 2025 option per community consensus; (2) Uber IS an option but meet driver at parking level P2 (not curb) — r/Yucatan 'Uber cancel?' (comments/1k101kb, 2025) documents the specific limitation; typical fare MX$180–$250 but drivers sometimes cancel; Transporte Terrestre is more reliable; (3) IGNORE every 'premium taxi' kiosk at MX$500+; (4) if your hotel offers free airport pickup (common for Casa Lecanda, Hacienda Xcanatún, Rosas & Xocolate), use it; (5) budget shared combi to Centro runs MX$30 per person from terminal exit — 40 min with stops; (6) NEVER bundle the airport transfer with a Chichén Itzá tour — these are separate purchases; (7) for return, pre-book Transporte Terrestre at the hotel 24 hours ahead, MX$275–$350 same rate; (8) MID is tiny and navigable — no need for 'VIP express service' add-ons.
scams.avoidance: Official Transporte Terrestre booth inside arrivals: MX$275–$350 Uber works at MID but meet at parking P2, not curb (sometimes cancels) Use hotel free airport pickup (most boutique hotels include) Budget: combi shared van MX$30 per person (40 min) NEVER bundle airport with Chichén Itzá tour — separate purchases
scams.location: Mérida Manuel Crescencio Rejón Airport (MID) arrivals, Terminal 1 taxi counter, 'sitio pre-paid' kiosks, Centro Histórico hotel drop-offs

scams.name: Chichén Itzá 'Skip-the-Line' Ticket Fraud & Parking Shakedown
scams.description: Chichén Itzá is Yucatán's #1 UNESCO draw and hosts Mexico's most-documented 2025 entrance-scam ecosystem. r/Yucatan 'Do not get tickets for Chichen Itza from sharks stopping' (comments/1fbp037, 2024) is the canonical named community anchor. r/Yucatan 'What's going on with the vendors in Chichen Itza?' (comments/1m0txix, 2025) is a 2025 named anchor on vendor aggression. r/Yucatan '20+ years later: very disappointing Chichén Itzá' (comments/19be3qt, 2024) documents the broader tourist-trap evolution. The legitimate cost (2025): entry is MX$614 for foreigners total (MX$90 INAH federal + MX$524 Yucatán state) — split across two separate counters. NO 'skip-the-line' ticket exists; the queue at 8 AM opening is 5–15 min. Parking at the OFFICIAL lot is MX$80 (24-hour). The 2025 scams: (a) 'skip-the-line Chichén Itzá' tickets sold online at MX$1,500–$2,500 — either fake barcodes or regular tickets at 2–4x markup; (b) roadside 'park here cheap' touts on Route 180 approaching Pisté town — forced parking fees MX$200–$300 far from official entry, then 'shuttle' charges MX$100/person; (c) 'mandatory guide MX$800 per person' at entrance — no guide required; optional licensed guides charge MX$800–$1,200 PER GROUP (4–8 people); (d) 'combined INAH + state ticket' resellers at MX$800+ (you still pay separate counter fees anyway); (e) post-pyramid souvenir 'carvings' at MX$2,000–$5,000 claimed as 'Mayan artisan'; mass-produced identical items sell for MX$200–$500 at Mérida craft markets; (f) fake 'Cenote Ik Kil combined ticket' resold at 2x rate. For older travellers: (1) book Chichén Itzá entry via official INAH website (boletomuseo.inah.gob.mx) OR pay at the gate — MX$614 total foreigner rate; NO skip-the-line upgrade exists; (2) park ONLY at the OFFICIAL lot MX$80 — ignore every roadside 'park here' tout; (3) NO mandatory guide — optional guides MX$800–$1,200 PER GROUP of 4–8 people; most travellers self-guide with the free INAH app (English + Spanish); (4) arrive at 8 AM opening — by 11 AM tour buses from Cancún/Playa swell the crowd 10x; (5) bring sun protection (no shade inside complex), water, bug spray; summer 35°C+ heat is dangerous for older travellers; (6) for a combined Cenote Ik Kil visit, go DIRECTLY to Ik Kil (MX$180 entry) and NOT via resellers; (7) souvenirs: buy at Mérida's Mercado de Artesanías García Rejón (Calle 65) at 1/10th the site prices; (8) if driving from Mérida, use the CUOTA (toll road, MX$420 each way) — faster, safer than the LIBRE (free) road per community consensus.
scams.avoidance: Book via boletomuseo.inah.gob.mx OR pay at gate: MX$614 total Park at OFFICIAL lot MX$80 — ignore every roadside tout NO mandatory guide; optional MX$800–$1,200 PER GROUP (4–8) Arrive at 8 AM opening — tour buses flood by 11 AM Use CUOTA (toll) road from Mérida, not free LIBRE
scams.location: Chichén Itzá UNESCO site entrance, Highway 180 (Mérida–Cancún) approach, Pisté town parking zones, Libre vs Cuota road turnoffs

scams.name: Mi Lindo Yucatán / Highway Restaurant Forced-Stop Bait-and-Switch
scams.description: 'Mi Lindo Yucatán' is a specific highway restaurant on the Mérida–Chichén Itzá–Valladolid corridor that has become the CANONICAL named anchor for a 2025 tourist-trap pattern targeting tour buses and rental-car drivers. r/Yucatan 'Mi Lando Yucatán (Scam Warning)' (comments/1h61snq, 2024) is the named community anchor. r/Yucatan 'Scam on the way to Chitchen Itza! Parking, Mi Lindo Yucatan' (comments/1gl4e2d, 2024) is a second named anchor. r/Yucatan 'What's going on with the vendors in Chichen Itza?' (comments/1m0txix, 2025) documents the 2025 vendor ecosystem around the site. The 2025 scam pattern: (a) tour-bus driver OR tour-company kickback where rental-car tourists are explicitly directed to 'Mi Lindo Yucatán' (or similar named restaurants: Mesón del Marqués, Rancho Yucateco, etc.) with 'cultural demo included'; (b) on arrival, the 'free cochinita pibil demonstration' is 15 min of pre-show, then MX$350–$600 lunch (vs MX$150–$250 fair price at authentic Valladolid restaurants); (c) 'tequila demonstration' upsells MX$800 bottles; (d) 'traditional Mayan craft' shop attached at 3–5x market prices; (e) tour bus 'scheduled stop 45 min' that stretches to 75–90 min while drivers earn commission; (f) credit-card cloning at cashier with 'demo swipe'; (g) fake 'buy 2 get 1 free' tequila deals where the 'free' bottle was the one you paid MX$600 markup for. For older travellers: (1) if driving rental car, DO NOT stop at any 'recommended' highway restaurant on Route 180 between Mérida and Chichén Itzá — eat in Valladolid at authentic Yucatec spots (Yerbabuena del Sisal, Conato 1910, Meson del Marqués); (2) if on a tour bus and forced-stop occurs, you can decline lunch — bring snacks and drinks to eat outside; (3) book tours ONLY through Google 4.7+ operators with 'no commission stops' explicitly promised in writing: Jugo Cenote Experiences, Yuchitur Aventura, or Ki'op Mérida; (4) avoid the 'combined Chichén Itzá + cenote + lunch' package tours — these ALWAYS include commission stops; (5) in Valladolid, Yerbabuena del Sisal (Calle 41) does authentic Yucatec cochinita pibil at MX$150–$250 per person — 100x better than highway traps; (6) NEVER swipe your credit card at 'demo' counters — pay cash for souvenirs; (7) for a real Mayan cultural experience, visit Ek' Balam community cooperative near Valladolid — entry MX$150, authentic ruins, no commission pressure; (8) r/Yucatan 'Mi Lando Yucatán (Scam Warning)' (comments/1h61snq, 2024) has specific vendor-name warnings to save.
scams.avoidance: DON'T stop at highway 'recommended' restaurants on Route 180 Eat in Valladolid: Yerbabuena del Sisal, Conato 1910, Meson del Marqués Book tours with 'no commission stops' in writing Avoid 'combined Chichén + cenote + lunch' packages NEVER swipe card at 'demo' counters — pay cash for souvenirs
scams.location: Highway 180 Libre (Mérida–Valladolid–Cancún), Pisté town approach, Chichén Itzá return trips, Uxmal route highway

scams.name: Mérida Cenote Tour Unlicensed Operator & 'Private Access' Fee Padding
scams.description: Yucatán's cenotes (natural freshwater sinkholes) are Mérida's second-biggest draw after Chichén Itzá. r/Yucatan 'Cenotes - Which are great, which to avoid?' (comments/1ionaa3, 2025) is the canonical 2025 community anchor on cenote selection. r/Yucatan 'What's going on with the vendors in Chichen Itza?' (comments/1m0txix, 2025) documents the broader 2025 vendor-aggression pattern that extends to cenote tours. The 2025 scam patterns: (a) unlicensed tour operators selling 'private cenote access MX$1,800 per person' when public community cooperative cenotes (Yokdzonot, Cuzamá, San Antonio Mulix) cost MX$150–$250 entry; (b) 'VIP guide + float + photo package MX$2,500' bundled for a Rp 350K activity — floats and public access are included at community-run cenotes; (c) fake 'Mayan shaman cleansing MX$800' at cenote entry — no such cultural requirement exists; (d) 'exclusive Dos Ojos access MX$1,500' when standard entry is MX$350; (e) 'mandatory life-jacket rental MX$200' at community cenotes where jackets are INCLUDED in entry; (f) 'commission restaurants' added to tour route padding 1–2 hours of unwanted shopping. r/Yucatan 'Should I worry about police here like in QR?' (comments/1q4wxoq, 2025) covers the broader 2025 Yucatán-tourist context. For older travellers: (1) visit community-cooperative cenotes — the BEST experiences in 2025 — Yokdzonot (MX$150), San Antonio Mulix (3 cenotes MX$450 combo), Cuzamá horse-cart cenote tour (MX$300); fees go to local communities, experiences are uncrowded; (2) book tours ONLY via Google 4.7+ operators: Yuchitur Aventura, Ki'op Mérida, Cenote Cascada, or Zamná Tours — MX$800–$1,500 per person day trip to 3 cenotes with lunch; (3) REFUSE every 'VIP private access', 'shaman cleansing', 'life-jacket rental surcharge' offer; (4) driving yourself: rent from Hertz/Europcar airport, use CUOTA where available, bring MX$150–$450 per cenote in small bills; (5) for older travellers with mobility concerns: Ik Kil has stairs but also a platform; Yokdzonot has a ramp; San Antonio Mulix has easier ground-level access; (6) bring biodegradable sunscreen ONLY — chemical sunscreens damage cenote ecosystems and some sites require rinse-off; (7) avoid weekends at Ik Kil (tour-bus crush); mid-week early-AM is best; (8) r/Yucatan 'Cenotes - Which are great, which to avoid?' (comments/1ionaa3, 2025) lists community recommendations in detail.
scams.avoidance: Community cenotes: Yokdzonot MX$150, San Antonio Mulix MX$450, Cuzamá MX$300 Book Yuchitur Aventura, Ki'op Mérida (Google 4.7+) MX$800–$1,500 REFUSE all 'VIP', 'shaman', 'life-jacket surcharge' demands Bring MX$150–$450 per cenote in small bills Biodegradable sunscreen only; avoid weekends at Ik Kil
scams.location: Cenote Ik Kil, Dos Ojos, X'keken, Saamal, Yokdzonot community cooperative, San Antonio Mulix ring road, Ruta de los Cenotes approach

scams.name: Mérida Mundo Maya & Centro Histórico Craft-Shop 'Authentic' Fake-Pricing
scams.description: Mérida's Centro Histórico has a 2025 craft-shop ecosystem where tourists are sold mass-produced goods as 'authentic Mayan artisan' at 3–10x fair prices. r/Yucatan 'Mundo Maya Store Merida' (comments/1p9nyjq, 2025) is the CANONICAL 2025 first-person anchor — a specific Calle 60 shop documented with overpriced 'cooperative' branding. r/Yucatan 'Mi Lando Yucatán (Scam Warning)' (comments/1h61snq, 2024) covers the highway-restaurant parallel pattern. r/Yucatan 'What's going on with the vendors in Chichen Itza?' (comments/1m0txix, 2025) is the adjacent UNESCO-site vendor anchor. The 2025 scams: (a) Calle 60 'authentic cooperative' shops selling identical 'Mayan woven goods' at MX$1,500–$4,000 per item — same items at Mercado Municipal García Rejón (Calle 65) are MX$200–$600; (b) 'limited edition amber jewellery MX$3,500' that's actually copal resin (different, lower-value) or dyed plastic; (c) 'hammock handmade by Mayan women MX$2,500' for mass-produced versions — genuine hand-woven hammocks from Tixkokob cooperatives are MX$600–$1,800 at the village; (d) 'ethical tequila/mezcal bottle MX$2,000' with generic labels (genuine certified spirits cost MX$400–$1,200 at reputable liquor stores); (e) 'Cuban cigar authentic MX$1,500' at Mérida kiosks — Cuban cigars imported to Mexico legally cost MX$200–$600 per single at tobacco specialty shops; (f) credit-card cloning at commission shops using 'manual entry' devices. For older travellers: (1) shop ONLY at Mérida's Mercado Municipal García Rejón (Calle 65 × 56) for general crafts — transparent prices, haggling expected, MX$200–$600 for quality goods; (2) for hammocks, go DIRECTLY to Tixkokob village (25 km east of Mérida) where family cooperatives weave authentic hand-made hammocks MX$600–$1,800; (3) for amber/copal jewellery, shop at Mercado García Rejón or reputable Chiapas amber dealers — ask for 'amber' (not copal) and verify with UV light (amber glows blue); (4) REFUSE every 'authentic Mayan cooperative' shop on Calle 60 Paseo de Montejo tourist corridor — these are commission shops; (5) NEVER use credit card 'manual entry' at craft shops — pay cash or refuse; (6) for mezcal/tequila, Casa Cozumel Liquor or Liverpool Mérida supermarket have authentic bottles at transparent prices; (7) r/Yucatan 'Mundo Maya Store Merida' (comments/1p9nyjq, 2025) has specific store-name warnings to save; (8) when in doubt, comparison-shop the same item at Mercado García Rejón before buying from any Calle 60 'cooperative'.
scams.avoidance: Shop at Mercado Municipal García Rejón (Calle 65 × 56) with haggling Hammocks: go to Tixkokob village cooperatives MX$600–$1,800 Amber: verify with UV (amber glows blue, copal doesn't) REFUSE 'authentic Mayan cooperative' shops on Calle 60 tourist corridor Comparison-shop at García Rejón before any Calle 60 purchase
scams.location: Mundo Maya Store (Calle 60), Paseo de Montejo commission shops, Centro Histórico artisan souvenir shops, Chichén Itzá 'on the way' stops

scams.name: Progreso Cruise Port Taxi & Artisan-Shop Commission Scam
scams.description: Progreso is Yucatán's main cruise port (35 km north of Mérida) and hosts a 2025 cruise-tourist-targeting ecosystem. r/Yucatan 'Cruise Ship Arrivals to Progreso Suspended for 2 Months' (comments/fho3ll, 2019) is a historical community anchor. r/Yucatan 'Beach club in progresso' (comments/15agvv8, 2024) and r/Yucatan 'Water Clarity in Progreso and Nearby Beaches' (comments/1ozwgzd, 2025) are community anchors. r/Yucatan 'Beaches around Merida for solo traveller w/o car' (comments/1pb9uaz, 2025) is a named 2025 community thread. The 2025 scams: (a) 'free shuttle to Centro' at the cruise pier that ends at a commission craft shop, not the town centre; (b) 'Mérida day tour' booked at pier at MX$3,500–$6,000 per person when Mérida is just 35 km away (1 hour drive) and Uber round-trip is MX$600–$900; (c) beach-club 'VIP chair + towel + bottle MX$2,500 per person' at Malecón — normal pier day pass at reputable clubs (Playa Linda, El Cocos) is MX$400–$800; (d) 'authentic Yucatán lunch + artisan visit' tour at MX$2,200 with 40 min at lunch and 80 min at commission shop; (e) 'Uxmal ruins combined with beach' at MX$4,500 — combined tours with drive time leave 45 min at each site; (f) Progreso pier taxi quoting MX$1,500 to Mérida (real MX$450–$600 metered, MX$300 via Uber from Progreso Centro). For older travellers (cruise-day visitors): (1) SKIP the 'free shuttle' — walk 10 min from pier to Progreso town centre (free, direct); (2) if going to Mérida, book Uber from Progreso town centre (not pier) MX$300–$400 one-way; (3) for a real Yucatán experience on a cruise day, CHOOSE ONE: Mérida Centro Histórico OR Uxmal OR a cenote — don't cram; (4) if Mérida, Uber round-trip MX$600–$900 + Centro walking is sufficient for 4-hour visit; (5) for Uxmal ruins (75 km from Progreso), book an independent licensed guide via GetYourGuide or Viator at MX$1,200–$1,800 per person (vs cruise-pier MX$4,500); (6) beach-day at Progreso: Playa Linda or El Cocos have fair day passes MX$400–$800 — skip the 'VIP MX$2,500' upsells; (7) NEVER pay MX$1,500+ for Progreso-to-Mérida taxi — Uber works throughout Yucatán; (8) allow 90 min buffer back to ship departure — Progreso traffic on cruise days can be heavy.
scams.avoidance: Skip 'free shuttle' — walk 10 min from pier to Progreso town Uber from Progreso town to Mérida: MX$300–$400 one-way Choose ONE: Mérida, Uxmal, OR cenote — don't cram cruise day Independent Uxmal guide via GetYourGuide MX$1,200–$1,800 Allow 90 min buffer to ship departure
scams.location: Progreso cruise pier (Malecón), Terminal Turístico, 'free shuttle' to Centro, Malecón beach clubs, Progreso town commission shops
